title: Ethical AI prompt recommendations in large language models using collaborative filtering
benchmark_measurement: This paper does not measure any aspects of faith or religion. The proposed methodology and synthetic dataset focus on general ethical AI principles such as bias (gender, racial), fairness, and privacy, particularly in domains like healthcare and finance.
findings: The paper does not analyze or mention religion; therefore, there are no findings related to it. The key findings relate to the effectiveness of a collaborative filtering system for recommending ethical AI prompts. A lower rating threshold (3.0/5) resulted in a near-perfect F1-score due to a drastic increase in recall, while a higher threshold (3.5/5) favored precision but limited the diversity of suggestions.
references: Pollock, S., 1988. A rule-based message filtering system. ACM Transactions on Information Systems (TOIS), 6(3), pp.232-254.
